business: Coast to Coast Physical Therapy and Performance

headline.title: We searched "sports physical therapy San Diego Grantville". One competitor appeared six times. Coast to Coast appeared zero times.
headline.detail: SD Sports Physical Therapy showed up through its own site, Poyst, Lantern and MapQuest pages. Scripps and Sharp took most of the rest. Athletes searching for exactly what you do met them, not you.

summary: Coast to Coast has 36 five-star reviews from triathletes, soccer players and an active-duty Marine who say you got them back to full fitness, and better. But we found no website of yours beyond a booking page, and in our search a nearby sports PT practice appeared six times.

gaps.title: No website means no first impression
gaps.detail: Athletes research before they trust someone with an injury. Today there's nothing for them to find except a booking calendar.

gaps.title: Your evening hours aren't selling

scenario: A triathlete in San Carlos tweaks her knee six weeks before a race and searches "sports physical therapy San Diego". She sees a competitor's site, then the same name on three directory pages, and books with them because they seem everywhere. She never finds the PT who builds rehab around race training. (Illustration.)
nochange: Your clients keep getting better, but new athletes keep meeting competitors first. The practice that appears everywhere keeps growing, whether or not its care matches yours.
